title: Face Sculpt #285 (한국 · 20대 · 눈물 글썽한 · 서큐버스 · 정면 · 유형 고유 메이크업 · P50 · 혼합 금속 추 9개/귀 1구멍 · 눈썹 대용 맨살 · 배경 실외 안개 낀 숲)
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, close-up beauty portrait. ONE woman, facing the camera straight on in a perfectly frontal portrait, her head level, both ears clearly visible on either side of her face, framed tightly from the very top of her head down to the line of her shoulders, the frame cutting off just below them, so the weights fully hang in view. Her face is large and sharp. Mid 20s.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful, seductive adult woman, mid 20s, a succubus brought to life: pale skin with real visible pores and a faint dusky flush on the cheekbones, two small, glossy, black, curved demon horns rising from her forehead at the hairline, long straight deep burgundy hair swept back behind both ears. Her eyes are large, sharp, heavy-lidded and seductive, with a long upturned wing of deep crimson liner, in violet contact lenses with vertical slit pupils, both eyes the same, fully opaque, with bright catchlights, under thin, sharp, high-arched black brows. Her lips are full, lush and glossy in a deep wine-black-red, with a pronounced cupid's bow, closed in a faint knowing smirk. High, sharp cheekbones, a slender nose and a defined jaw. A dangerous, seductive, confident gaze straight into the camera. Every feature is exaggerated but beautiful, balanced and refined, in harmony with the rest of her face, never distorted, never grotesque. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain and a soft sheen of natural oils, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real woman's face, not an illustration, not a render. She has no eyebrows at all: her brow bones are completely smooth, bare, clean skin with no hair, no drawing and no ornament, like the face of the Mona Lisa, so the whole attention rests on her eyes.

Piercings: A face fully covered with real piercings, about thirty-four in total (not counting the hanging weights), spread over every area so that no area is empty: a single large septum ring of different sizes and shapes through the thin soft wall between the nostrils, in a short stack that ends above the upper lip; one small ring wrapping snugly around each nostril wing; two small ring or studs on the chin; on each ear, one large healed opening in the earlobe holding a very thick, heavy black cast-iron ring as thick as a finger, a plain solid ring with no open tunnel, and above it sit seven pieces above the lobe: four classic round O-rings and studs along the helix rim, two studs and small bars across the upper cartilage and one in the conch and tragus; five small studs across the lower half of the forehead just above the brows in even rows, leaving the upper forehead free; four small studs along each cheekbone, well clear of the eyes. The left and right sides are balanced. The pieces are spread over the whole face in clear rows so every one reads individually, with bare skin between them; the eyes and eyelids stay clear. All the ear weights hang from the bottoms of this iron ring, and they are not counted in the piercing total: on each ear there are exactly nine separate massive weights, each of a different shape and a different metal, all of them rough, hammered, matte and unpolished, each hanging on its own thick heavy chain of the same metal as the weight: on the left ear rough-cast matte yellow gold a barrel-shaped weight on a shortest chain, dark patinated bronze a hammer head on a shortest chain, dull dark brass a cube-shaped block on a short chain, blackened cast iron a miniature anvil on a medium chain, tarnished dark silver a teardrop-shaped sinker on a medium chain, dull blue-grey lead a pyramid-shaped lump on a long chain, oxidized dark copper a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre on a longer chain, dull pewter-grey tin a square-sided cowbell on a longer chain, rough-cast matte yellow gold a ship's anchor on a longest chain; on the right ear rough-cast matte yellow gold a teardrop-shaped sinker on a shortest chain, dull blue-grey lead a bell-shaped weight like a small temple bell with a flared rim on a shortest chain, oxidized dark copper a round bell on a short chain, dark patinated bronze a pyramid-shaped lump on a medium chain, dull pewter-grey tin a cube-shaped block on a medium chain, tarnished dark silver a square-sided cowbell on a long chain, dull dark brass a miniature anvil on a longer chain, blackened cast iron a ship's anchor on a longer chain, dark patinated bronze a hammer head on a longest chain. On each ear the single iron ring carries all the weights, hanging in a staggered cluster on chains of different lengths and staggered at different heights so every weight is fully visible and none hides another. Every single weight is a massive, dense, solid lump of metal at least as big as her whole fist and clearly larger than her earlobe, rough and matte and unpolished with no shine and no delicate or thin parts; its size does NOT shrink just because there are many of them: the last weight is exactly as big, as thick and as heavy-looking as the first. Each weight alone looks like it weighs several kilograms, each chain is pulled bar-straight and taut, and at a glance every single one looks crushingly, unmistakably heavy, the chains hanging freely in the air, clear of her neck and shoulders, with even the longest chain and its weight ending no lower than the level of her collarbones, never below them and never resting on her chest or body. Because all the load is carried by one opening, the weight gently pulls each earlobe down a little into a slightly elongated, soft, healthy loop of skin, only a small natural droop that is just enough to show how heavy the weights are; the lobe never stretches long, never tears or collapses and never hangs down to her neck or shoulder, her head stays upright, and the skin stays smooth and intact, fully healed, with no tearing, no wound, no blood and no redness. The face and ear jewelry is real blackened steel set with small clear diamonds, one-colour, restrained, while the hanging weights are always rough, matte, unpolished heavy metal in mixed materials (lead, tin, gold, silver, bronze, copper, brass and iron), sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Hair: her hair is swept back behind both ears, leaving both ears, her jawline and her neck fully visible so every hanging piece is in clear view.

Lighting: The background is a misty forest at dusk, soft blurred dark-green trees fading into pale fog, out of focus with a shallow depth of field, with no objects and no people in the background, and the background is darker and softer than her face so that her face and the metal are the brightest, sharpest part of the image. The background colours are cool, mid-to-dark tones clearly different from her skin tone, never beige, peach, orange or brown, and never bright. A soft frontal light on her face and ears, so the glints on every piece of metal read clearly against her skin; a thin cool rim light along the hair and shoulders. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
